project: Investor Emotions and Stock Market Behaviour

observations.01_emotion_distribution: Optimism is the dominant emotion with 1624 posts (16.2%), followed by excitement (1386) and anxiety (1366), whereas depression (205) and surprise (244) represent the rarest classes.
observations.02_bullish_vs_bearish: Investor sentiment leans distinctly bullish with 5,474 posts (54.7%) compared to 4,526 bearish posts (45.3%), reflecting retail equity bias.
observations.03_emotion_x_sentiment: Optimism and excitement are over 98% bullish, whereas disgust (94.9%), anxiety (89.5%), panic (97.7%), and depression (98.5%) align almost strictly with bearish sentiment; neutral categories (ambiguous, surprise) exhibit mixed polarity.
observations.04_posts_per_ticker: Retail tweet volume exhibits severe concentration: TSLA alone accounts for 4341 posts (43.4%), and the top 3 tickers (TSLA, AAPL, BA) comprise 69.8% of all posts.
observations.05_emotion_by_ticker_top10: Growth and tech leaders (TSLA, AAPL, AMZN) show strong positive emotion majorities (over 40-50%), whereas pandemic-disrupted aerospace and cruise operators (BA: 42.9% negative; CCL: 45.1% negative) exhibit substantial negative sentiment spikes.
observations.06_monthly_emotion_trend_with_sp500: Negative emotions surged in March 2020 (443 posts) matching the S&P 500 COVID-19 market drawdown to 2,584, followed by positive emotions rebounding strongly as equity markets climbed to record highs through Q3 and Q4 2020.
observations.07_text_length_distribution: Tweet lengths follow a right-skewed distribution with a median of 66 characters and 13 words; values exceeding 174.5 characters (4.95%) or 34 words (4.23%) qualify as statistical outliers by IQR.
observations.08_emotion_group_distribution: Positive emotions represent the largest group (4,736 posts, 47.4%), followed by negative emotions (3,540 posts, 35.4%) and neutral emotions (1,724 posts, 17.2%).
observations.09_monthly_bullish_share_vs_sp500: Retail bullish sentiment fell to a 2020 low in March (46.8% bullish) as equity indices collapsed, subsequently rising past 60% in autumn alongside the broader market recovery.

conclusion.findings: Emotion features do not outperform the majority baseline out-of-sample (Logistic Regression accuracy 50.85% vs. Majority Baseline 52.56%). Consistent with weak-form market efficiency, retail social sentiment reflects contemporaneous price activity but lacks predictive return forecasting power.
